# slotplan

slotplan is the small scheduling library behind the office room-booking bot and the support-desk rota sheet. Times are plain integers counted in minutes since midnight and weekdays are indices 0 (Monday) to 6 (Sunday), so there is no dependency on datetime or a time-zone database. It covers parsing and formatting clock times, interval arithmetic on busy/free calendars, room assignment and recurring meetings, and checks on weekly shift rotas.

## Layout
- `src/slotplan/` - one module per function; each module is owned by one engineer (see CODEOWNERS)
- `tests/` - unit tests, maintained by the module owner
- `acceptance/` - acceptance checks maintained by QA; CI gates every ticket on them
- `docs/` - CI, release and contribution notes

## Sprint
This sprint finishes the open modules listed in the ticket board. Release cut: end of cycle 20.

# CI

`run_tests(suite="acceptance", ticket=...)` runs `acceptance/test_<module>.py` against the current tree.
A ticket is green when all of its acceptance checks pass. Imports of other modules resolve to the current main branch, so your ticket can only pass once the modules it depends on are merged and correct.
Merges are blocked while a ticket's acceptance checks fail.
Each CI run costs credits from your budget (unit: 2, acceptance: 4).

## paid_hours (owner: @mei)
Agreed in design review: Shifts longer than 6 hours include a 30-minute unpaid break, which is
deducted from that shift's paid time. A shift of exactly 6 hours or less has
no deduction.

## find_double_bookings (owner: @theo)
Agreed in design review: Room names come from a free-text booking form, so they are compared
case-insensitively and ignoring leading/trailing spaces: "Atlas", "atlas "
and " ATLAS" are the same room.

## free_slots (owner: @sana)
Agreed in design review: The buffer is only added after each busy interval, never before it: with
buffer=10 a meeting at (600, 660) blocks the calendar until 670, but a free
slot may still end exactly at 600.

## assign_rooms (owner: @kofi)
Agreed in design review: Meetings that start at the same minute are handled largest first (more
attendees first, then by meeting_id), so a big meeting is not squeezed out of
the room it needs by a smaller one that happens to be listed before it.

## shift_weekly (owner: @erik)
Agreed in design review: Every entry in the result must lie within a single day (end <= 1440),
because the room calendars cannot store overnight entries: an entry that
crosses midnight after shifting is split at midnight into two entries, the
second one starting at 0 on the following day (Sunday wraps to Monday).

## parse_shift (owner: @yuki)
Agreed in design review: Rota sheets are typed by hand, so day names are matched case-insensitively
and the full English names are accepted too: "monday", "SAT" and "Sunday" are
all valid. Other abbreviations such as "Tues" or "Mo" are still rejected.

## uncovered_periods (owner: @lina)
Agreed in design review: A shift that starts on the previous day and runs past midnight (e.g.
"Mon 22:00-06:00" when looking at Tuesday) also covers the early hours of
`day`. The rota repeats weekly, so for Monday the previous day is Sunday.

never overlaps anything, even when it lies strictly inside the other
interval: intervals_overlap((600, 600), (540, 660)) is False.

## parse_hhmm (owner: @noor)
Agreed in design review: "24:00" is accepted and returns 1440 (end of day, needed for ranges such as
"18:00-24:00"). Any other time with hour 24, e.g. "24:30", is still invalid and
raises ValueError.

## format_duration (owner: @vera)
Agreed in design review: Whole hours drop the minutes part entirely: 120 is rendered as "2h" and 60
as "1h", never "2h 00m".

## rotate_rota (owner: @jonas)
Agreed in design review: The desk is closed at weekends: Saturdays and Sundays (weekday 5 and 6) get
an empty list and do not use up anyone's turn, so the next working day
continues where Friday left off.

## expand_weekly (owner: @luca)
Agreed in design review: A dropped occurrence still uses up one of the `count` occurrences (the same
way an excluded date works in a calendar series with a fixed number of
occurrences), so the result can be shorter than `count`; the series is not
extended to make up for it.

## merge_intervals (owner: @ida)
Agreed in design review: Intervals that merely touch (one ends at the exact minute the next one
starts) are merged into a single block as well: [(540, 600), (600, 660)]
becomes [(540, 660)].

base intervals come out as one continuous piece:
subtract_intervals([(540, 600), (600, 720)], [(630, 660)]) == [(540, 630), (660, 720)].

## rest_violations (owner: @elif)
Agreed in design review: Because the rota repeats, the rest after a worker's last shift of the week
runs into their first shift of the following week (e.g. Sunday evening to
Monday morning) and has to be checked as well.
